payoff: Select exactly two high-value hypothetical banking E2E journeys, route seven technical regression cases downward and distinguish smoke, regression and acceptance without installing a browser.
learningOutcomes: pilih 2 high-value E2E flows (login→view balance, login→transfer→receipt); jelaskan kasus kompleks yang sebaiknya tetap di API/integration tests.
mentalModel: User-value cross-system workflows -> two E2E smoke; technical edge cases -> unit/API/contract/service integration; acceptance = observable outcomes across layers.
relationshipGraph: TST-019 contract -> TST-021 Pact -> TST-022 provider fault -> TST-023 adversarial inputs -> TST-024 DB integration -> TST-025 E2E selection -> TST-026 browser smoke implementation.

concepts.title: High-value user journey selection
concepts.mechanism: Retain end-to-end checks for login to balance and login to transfer to receipt because they cross authentication, navigation and user-visible business output.

concepts.title: Cheapest faithful test boundary
concepts.mechanism: Place fee rounding in unit, malformed status and pagination in API, contract drift in contract, and timeout/persisted UNKNOWN in service integration.

concepts.title: Smoke vs regression vs acceptance
concepts.mechanism: Smoke is a narrow high-value release signal; regression includes broader lower-layer cases; acceptance states observable business outcomes, not a synonym for browser automation.

misconceptions: More E2E browser edge cases do not automatically improve confidence or signal quality.
A transfer receipt marked PENDING does not prove financial settlement.
Provider timeout and idempotency need real HTTP/database integration checks, not extra browser tests.
Smoke, regression and business acceptance are different test purposes, not synonyms.
The Node selection fixture does not execute Playwright, bank UI, login or actual user journeys.
practice: Define login→balance and login→transfer→receipt with observable end conditions and isolated fixtures.
Map fee rounding, invalid login, pagination, malformed payload, idempotency replay, API drift and provider timeout to cheaper faithful test stages.
Review smoke/regression/acceptance distinctions and reject accidental new E2E cases or production dependencies using the Node fixture.

coverage.taughtAt: Three V3 segments teach critical journey selection, lower-layer boundary allocation and smoke/regression/acceptance
coverage.assessedAt: Five questions and standalone deterministic Node selection audit with negative mutation guards
coverage.evidenceExpected: Exactly two proposed E2E workflows with observable results; seven lower-layer test scenarios placed in unit, API, contract or integration; no browser execution claim.

coverage.taughtAt: Independent ticketing/checkout selection plus scenario boundary and isolation exercise
coverage.assessedAt: Project exercise plus Node test matrix assertions for selected E2E, fake dependencies and rejected invalid plan variants
coverage.evidenceExpected: A small test strategy with two high-value journeys, lower-layer negative coverage and explicit data isolation without external production requests.

segments.objective: Select exactly two valuable end-to-end user journeys with observable outcomes and no unnecessary test duplication.
segments.whyItMatters: UI E2E tests are expensive and fragile; excessive coverage obscures the critical release signal.
segments.mentalModel: Select a user-visible cross-system outcome, not one browser test per validation branch.
segments.explanation: For a hypothetical bank application, journey one is login → view balance and journey two is login → transfer → receipt. Both cross authentication and navigation to a business outcome visible to a user. The receipt shows a created/PENDING transfer reference, not completed bank settlement. This selection is a design exercise: CS-101 itself is a read-only educational library, with no login or banking UI. The executable fixture checks this proposed selection; it does not launch a browser.

workedExample.problem: An engineer proposes a browser E2E for every pagination and currency validation error.

steps.action: List two highest-value full user tasks: balance access and transfer receipt.
steps.reason: These combine important behavior that a single API assertion cannot prove from the user's perspective.

steps.action: Write visible end conditions for each one.
steps.reason: An E2E smoke must prove the user reached the intended outcome.
steps.expectedResult: Balance amount visible; receipt reference and PENDING status visible.

guidedPractice.prompt: Which is a stronger E2E selection: checking limit=-1 in ten browsers, or login→transfer→receipt once?
hints: Choose a complete user value path.
Negative query bounds are testable without a browser.
guidedPractice.explanation: Retain login→transfer→receipt as the critical E2E; test invalid limits in API tests.

independentChallenge.prompt: Choose two minimal journeys for a ticketing service: login→see ticket and login→buy ticket→confirmation; state a distinct observable result for each.
expectedEvidence: Exactly two user-value journeys, each with a visible final assertion and no redundant validation branches.
independentChallenge.variationFromExample: Ticketing purchase rather than banking transfer.

segments.firstAction: Write the balance journey in three steps.

misconceptionRepair.likelyMistake: Counting dozens of browser edge cases as automatically stronger reliability.
misconceptionRepair.whyItFails: It creates fragile duplication while missing a concise business-value signal.
misconceptionRepair.correctiveAction: Reserve E2E for critical cross-system user paths; prove edge cases at lower boundaries.

selfCheck.expectedObservation: Two E2E candidates remain: login→balance and login→transfer→receipt.
selfCheck.ifUnexpected: Check whether each candidate includes both authentication and a user-visible business result.

continueFromHere.nextAction: Route lower-value validation and failure cases to lower test layers.
continueFromHere.resumeCue: Start from the two real user goals, not framework test types.

segments.objective: Classify complex validation and failure cases into unit, API, contract or service-integration tests rather than E2E.
segments.whyItMatters: A lower-level test often reproduces a failure more reliably, with faster diagnostics and isolated dependencies.
segments.mentalModel: Place the assertion at the cheapest real boundary that can observe the failure.
segments.explanation: Decimal rounding belongs to unit tests. Unsupported pagination and invalid amounts belong to API tests. OpenAPI field-type drift belongs to contract testing. Idempotency key replay and provider timeout/UNKNOWN persistence belong to real service and database integration tests. These choices build on TST-019 through TST-024 and should not be duplicated as browser E2E matrix rows. API/integration tests remain necessary alongside two browser journeys.

workedExample.problem: The provider times out after receiving a debit; QA suggests 15 browser cases to inspect UNKNOWN outcomes.

steps.action: Identify whether browser navigation is essential to observe the failure.
steps.reason: Provider timeout and persisted state are primarily service-boundary contracts.
steps.expectedResult: The failure can be proven through HTTP requests, stub call counts and SQL rows.

steps.action: Assign the provider timeout case to service integration, and field-type drift to contract tests.
steps.reason: Keep E2E tests narrowly focused on visible user journey outcomes.
steps.expectedResult: All technical edge cases have an owner below E2E.

guidedPractice.prompt: Where should a same-key/different-amount HTTP 409 with one DB record be verified?
hints: This requires request replay and persisted state.
A browser cannot make the SQL invariants clearer than the service test.
guidedPractice.explanation: At API/service integration, with the stable 409 response and a direct state assertion.

independentChallenge.prompt: Route a duplicate ticket checkout, 503 ticket provider timeout, and tax rounding to the cheapest faithful test boundaries.
expectedEvidence: A rationale-based mapping with duplicate checkout in integration, timeout in integration, and rounding in unit.
independentChallenge.variationFromExample: Ticketing provider instead of bank provider.

segments.firstAction: Pick one failure case and name the layer that can verify its invariant.

misconceptionRepair.likelyMistake: Assuming browser E2E is required because the failure has business impact.
misconceptionRepair.whyItFails: Business risk matters, but the test boundary should match where the invariant is observable.
misconceptionRepair.correctiveAction: Retain one E2E happy path and move boundary-specific failure branches into focused tests.

selfCheck.expectedObservation: No negative pagination, malformed JSON, idempotency conflict, contract drift or timeout case is classified as a new E2E.
selfCheck.ifUnexpected: Ask whether a user-visible navigation step is essential to reproduce each assertion.

continueFromHere.nextAction: Define what smoke, regression and acceptance each mean in a release.
continueFromHere.resumeCue: Resume with the cheapest faithful test boundary rule.

segments.objective: Distinguish a two-journey smoke gate from the broad regression suite and from business acceptance criteria.
segments.whyItMatters: If all tests are called E2E or acceptance, a team cannot keep CI fast or interpret failures.
segments.mentalModel: Smoke = critical narrow release signal; regression = broader change protection; acceptance = observable business criteria across layers.
segments.explanation: The two chosen journeys are proposed browser smoke cases for a future bank UI. Their acceptance conditions are 'balance visible for an authenticated account' and 'receipt reference/status visible after transfer'. Regression cases include unit/API/contract/integration tests for rounding, auth, invalid amount, pagination, idempotency, drift and timeout persistence. For the bank mutation journey, seed a unique test account and fake external provider; avoid production credentials and shared mutable accounts. Browser automation and any real bank UI are intentionally deferred to TST-026 and later.

workedExample.problem: A smoke suite fails because the transfer test reuses an account changed by the previous test.

steps.action: Use a dedicated seeded account per mutating scenario and isolate browser state.
steps.reason: Tests must not depend on execution order or prior balances.

steps.action: Define release smoke separately from broad regression and acceptance statements.
steps.reason: Different evidence tiers answer different questions.
steps.expectedResult: Two proposed E2E smoke journeys, multiple lower-level regression checks, and two visible acceptance conditions.

guidedPractice.prompt: Does passing two proposed E2E smoke flows prove every debit edge case is correct?
hints: Smoke is a narrow high-value signal.
API, contract and database integration tests still own complex edge cases.
guidedPractice.explanation: No. Smoke is only a critical workflow check, not a substitute for regression or financial settlement evidence.

independentChallenge.prompt: Plan seeded, isolated state for two checkout flows with one purchase receipt, and state what is excluded from browser smoke.
expectedEvidence: Independent account/fixture scope, observable receipt criteria and delegated API/integration negative tests.
independentChallenge.variationFromExample: Checkout and receipt with isolated inventory instead of bank account balance.

segments.firstAction: Write the user-visible acceptance criterion for balance and receipt.

misconceptionRepair.likelyMistake: Treating two browser smoke passes as evidence of full production readiness or financial correctness.
misconceptionRepair.whyItFails: They do not cover provider edge cases, ledger settlement or concurrency guarantees.
misconceptionRepair.correctiveAction: Keep separate regression/integration coverage and explicitly state the smoke evidence limit.

selfCheck.expectedObservation: Exactly two proposed E2E smoke cases, lower-layer regression coverage and independent test-data plans.
selfCheck.ifUnexpected: Inspect each test's data ownership and whether it claims business effects beyond visible UI.

continueFromHere.nextAction: Implement a browser smoke only when a real local banking UI exists and the next curriculum unit requires it.
continueFromHere.resumeCue: Remember smoke, regression and acceptance answer different questions.
